---
title: "Lighttable"
subtitle: "A companion app for image-set triage — the digital contact sheet before the figure"
---

Lighttable is a small, fast desktop app that ships in the Flux repository as a **companion**
— not one of Flux's modes, but the step *before* them. Analysis batches produce piles of
images: a parameter sweep at five settings, per-cell outputs across conditions, one plot per
model. Lighttable is the light table you spread them on: a grid of every image in one
variant, **instant flipping between variants** (each cell swaps in place, like a flip-book),
fullscreen inspection, and side-by-side comparison of one item across every variant.

You explore the many in Lighttable; you [compose the chosen few in Flux](modes/figure.qmd).

# How it thinks: collections, sets, items

Lighttable opens a **collection** — a plain folder whose subfolders are **sets** (one per
variant), each holding one image per **item**, aligned by filename:

```
sweep/                        ← the collection (the folder you open)
├── smoothing-0.1/            ← a set: one variant of the batch
│   ├── cell_007.png          ← an item, keyed by its filename
│   ├── cell_012.png
│   └── …
├── smoothing-0.5/            ← another set — same item filenames
│   ├── cell_007.png
│   └── …
└── smoothing-2.0/
    └── …
```

The alignment is the whole trick: `smoothing-0.1/cell_007.png` and
`smoothing-2.0/cell_007.png` are *the same cell*, so switching sets flips every image in
place. A set missing an item shows a placeholder — the grid never shifts, so partial sets
are fine. Sets are flat (no nesting inside), loose images in the collection root form an
"All" set, and the usual image formats work (PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG, GIF, AVIF, BMP). Name
items consistently and zero-pad (`cell_007`, not `cell_7`) — sorting is natural everywhere.

Making a collection is ordinary analysis code: loop conditions × items and save each image
to `<collection>/<condition>/<item>.png`. Plain matplotlib is fine here — these are triage
images, not blessed figures. When a winner emerges, regenerate it properly
[via fluxplot into the project's `plots/`](concepts/semantic-plots.qmd).

# Running it

Lighttable runs from the Flux **source checkout** (it isn't bundled into the packaged app):

```bash
cd ~/flux/lighttable         # or wherever you cloned Flux
npm ci                       # first run only — exact install from the committed lockfile
npm start -- ~/sweep         # build + run, opening the collection
```

`npm start` **is** `npm run build && electron .`, so there's no separate build step to run
before it. If you only want Flux's top-bar Lighttable button to work and don't need to open
it right now, `npm run build` on its own is the alternative — the button launches it for you.

The sidecar has its **own** dependencies and build, entirely separate from Flux's — run
these from inside `lighttable/`, never from the repo root.

Once it's open you can also drop a folder onto the window, use the Open picker, or pick
from Recents.

From inside Flux, the Lighttable button on the right side of the top bar (next to the Docs
button and Settings gear) launches it directly — a fresh window if it isn't running, or the existing one
brought to front. The button needs the one-time `npm ci` plus a build — either `npm run
build`, or one `npm start`, which builds on its way up. If either is missing it tells you
which.

# Using it

**The grid.** Arrow keys move; **Enter** (or clicking a cell) opens the image fullscreen;
**1–9** jump straight to set N and **Tab** cycles sets — this is the flip-book. **[** and
**]** change the column count, **/** searches items, **c** toggles filename captions, and
**Escape** backs out of whatever you're in.

**Detail view** (fullscreen one image): **←/→** step through items (skipping gaps),
**↑/↓** flip sets *without leaving the image*, **Enter** toggles fit vs. 1:1, **-/=** zoom.

**Compare view**: **Ctrl+click** a cell (or **Ctrl+Enter**) lays out that one item across
**all** sets at once, tiles packed as large as they fit and captioned by set name — the
"which smoothing do I believe?" view. Click a tile to fullscreen it; **Escape** steps back.

**Sister collections**: click the collection name (top-left) to see the folders sitting
*beside* the current one and switch with one click — so `triage/monday_sweep/`,
`triage/tuesday_sweep/` becomes one-click history. **Ctrl+click** the name for the folder
picker. Grid spacing is adjustable in the **⋯** menu.

# Where it stops

Lighttable knows nothing about Flux projects — no captions, no manifests, no citations,
just folders of images, kept deliberately separate so it stays instant at any batch size.
When an image graduates from "candidate" to "figure panel", that's your cue to leave the
light table: regenerate it with [fluxplot](concepts/semantic-plots.qmd) and build the real
thing in [Figure mode](modes/figure.qmd).

# Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause → fix |
|---|---|
| `npm start` fails immediately | Dependencies not installed → `npm ci` inside `lighttable/` first |
| Flux's Lighttable button says the Electron binary is missing | Electron's postinstall download didn't finish (`npm ci` succeeded, but `lighttable/node_modules/electron/` has no `dist/`) → `node node_modules/electron/install.js` inside `lighttable/` |
| No Lighttable on this machine | It needs the source checkout — packaged Flux doesn't bundle it ([Installation](installation.qmd)) |
| Cells shift when flipping sets | Item filenames differ between sets → align the names (same key per item in every set) |
| Wrong order (`cell_10` before `cell_7`) | Un-padded numbers → zero-pad the filenames |
